findings.highlight: Mari-san's weird changes in her attitude really perplex me sometimes, and I still can't understand her completely to this day
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんの、その妙に言い訳がましい態度の意味は、今の俺には、よく意味がわからなかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki does not understand, at this moment, why Mari is acting strangely defensive—as though making excuses—after volunteering that her traveling companion is not a man. The English turns that specific romantic tell into a timeless general claim that Mari's changing moods sometimes perplex him, erasing both the excuse-like behavior and its immediate cause.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの、その妙に言い訳がましい態度の意味は、
今の俺には、よく意味がわからなかった。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san's weird changes in her attitude really perplex me sometimes, and I still can't understand her completely to this day.

findings.highlight: The moment I finally manage to keep up with the conversation, a name appears that makes my head go completely blank once again…
findings.evidenceJa:
やっと普通に声が出るようになってきたところに、
また頭を真っ白にしてくれる名字がこぼれ出た…
findings.explanation: Haruki had only just regained an ordinary speaking voice when Touma's surname blanks his mind again; the English says he had managed to keep up with the conversation.
findings.japanese:
やっと普通に声が出るようになってきたところに、
また頭を真っ白にしてくれる名字がこぼれ出た…
findings.todokanai: The moment I finally manage to keep up with the conversation, a name appears that makes my head go completely blank once again…

findings.highlight: You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara?
findings.evidenceJa: 北原って結構ナイーブだよな。傷つきやすくて、自分で自分を責めてばかりで
findings.explanation: ナイーブ is immediately glossed by Mari as emotionally sensitive: Haruki is easily hurt and constantly blames himself. 'Naive' instead calls him inexperienced or gullible, assigning a different character flaw and breaking the explanatory relation to her next sentence.
findings.japanese:
「北原って結構ナイーブだよな。
傷つきやすくて、自分で自分を責めてばかりで」
findings.todokanai: "You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara? You're quite fragile, and you always seem to only put the blame on yourself."

findings.highlight: Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も、自分を叱ってくれないから。…叱った後、許してくれないから
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether Haruki sinks further because no one will scold him—and, after scolding him, forgive him. The English changes this into Haruki having nobody from whom he can request forgiveness, weakening Mari's insight that he wants punishment administered by someone who will then absolve him.
findings.japanese:
「だから余計落ち込むのか？
誰も、自分を叱ってくれないから。
…叱った後、許してくれないから」
findings.todokanai: "Is that why you got so depressed? Because there was nobody to reprimand you for it? Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward…?"

findings.highlight: "I've always been in love with Touma Kazusaーeven now."
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺、冬馬かずさのこと、今でも好きだったんです」
findings.explanation: Haruki confesses that he discovered he was still in love with Kazusa; 'I've always been in love' makes the continuity more absolute.
findings.japanese: 「俺、冬馬かずさのこと、今でも好きだったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I've always been in love with Touma Kazusaーeven now."

findings.highlight: "Well, I don't mean anything bad by all that. Perhaps it's better to say you're a bit too composed, too argumentative, and too conscious of things sometimes?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ま、悪い意味じゃないよ。
落ち着きすぎてるって言うか、
理屈っぽいって言うか、醒めてるって言うか」
findings.explanation: Mari calls Haruki overcomposed, argumentative, and emotionally detached or cynical; the English renders the last trait as overly conscious.
findings.japanese:
「ま、悪い意味じゃないよ。
落ち着きすぎてるって言うか、
理屈っぽいって言うか、醒めてるって言うか」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I don't mean anything bad by all that. Perhaps it's better to say you're a bit too composed, too argumentative, and too conscious of things sometimes?"
